## R code

```{r}
# power for a treatment effect of 5 and a standard error of 2 (the case in Figure 1)
tau <- 5
se  <- 2

# Rule 1: the normal CDF with mean tau and standard deviation SE
1 - pnorm(1.64*se, mean = tau, sd = se)

# Rule 2: the standard normal CDF (the same number)
1 - pnorm(1.64 - tau/se)
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Check by simulation

::: {.panel-tabset group="simulation"}
### Base R

```{r}
#| label: sim-figure-1-base-r
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# simulate the case in Figure 1: a treatment effect of 5 and a standard error of 2; any design
#   with that standard error will do, here 50 respondents per condition and outcomes with an SD
#   of 10 within each condition (Rule 3); analyze each experiment as in the paper (OLS with HC2
#   standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors
library(lmtest)    # confidence intervals with robust standard errors

set.seed(1234)
n    <- 50
sd_y <- 10
tau  <- 5

simulate_experiment <- function() {
  y0  <- rnorm(2*n, mean = 0, sd = sd_y)   # potential outcomes under control...
  y1  <- y0 + tau                          # ...and under treatment
  z   <- sample(rep(0:1, each = n))        # n respondents to each condition, at random
  y   <- ifelse(z == 1, y1, y0)
  fit <- lm(y ~ z)
  v   <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")
  ci  <- coefci(fit, "z", level = 0.90, vcov. = v, df = Inf)
  c(se = sqrt(v["z", "z"]), reject = ci[1] > 0)
}
sims <- replicate(5000, simulate_experiment())

# the average standard error (2) and the share of rejections (Rules 1 and 2: 80%)
rowMeans(sims)
```

### DeclareDesign

The design follows [Declaration 18.1](https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html) in Blair, Coppock, and Humphreys ([2023](#ref-Blair2023)).

```{r}
#| label: sim-figure-1-declaredesign
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# the case in Figure 1 as a design: a treatment effect of 5 and a standard error of 2 (50
#   respondents per condition and outcomes with an SD of 10 within each condition; Rule 3);
#   analyze each experiment as in the paper (the difference in means, with HC2 standard errors;
#   reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(DeclareDesign)

n    <- 50
sd_y <- 10
tau  <- 5

figure_1 <-
  declare_model(N = 2 * n,
                U = rnorm(N, sd = sd_y),
                potential_outcomes(Y ~ tau * Z + U)) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5)) +
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z, inquiry = "ATE", alpha = 0.10)

# the average standard error (2) and the share of rejections (Rules 1 and 2: 80%)
set.seed(1234)
diagnose_design(figure_1, sims = 5000, bootstrap_sims = FALSE,
                diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
                  se = mean(std.error),
                  power = mean(conf.low > 0)))
```
:::
:::

## R code

```{r}
# minimum detectable effect, in standard errors
qnorm(0.95) + qnorm(0.80)   # one-sided test, 80% power (2.5)
qnorm(0.95) + qnorm(0.95)   # one-sided test, 95% power (3.3)
qnorm(0.975) + qnorm(0.80)  # two-sided test, 80% power (2.8)
qnorm(0.975) + qnorm(0.95)  # two-sided test, 95% power (3.6)

# footnote 22: the inverse of the standard normal CDF at 0.80
qnorm(0.80)

# error from rounding 2.48 to 2.5 and 3.29 to 3.3 (%): MDE and sample size
mde_80 <- qnorm(0.95) + qnorm(0.80)
mde_95 <- qnorm(0.95) + qnorm(0.95)
100*abs(c(2.5/mde_80, 3.3/mde_95) - 1)
100*abs(c(2.5/mde_80, 3.3/mde_95)^2 - 1)
```
:::

## Check by simulation

### Base R

```{r}
#| label: sim-ahler-sood-base-r
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# simulate the replication: 500 respondents per condition, outcomes with an SD of 20.8 within
#   each condition, and a treatment effect of 3.30 (the 80% MDE from Rule 5); analyze each
#   experiment as in the paper (OLS with HC2 standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the
#   90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors
library(lmtest)    # confidence intervals with robust standard errors

set.seed(1234)
n    <- 500
sd_y <- 20.8
tau  <- 3.30  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

simulate_experiment <- function() {
  y0  <- rnorm(2*n, mean = 0, sd = sd_y)   # potential outcomes under control...
  y1  <- y0 + tau                          # ...and under treatment
  z   <- sample(rep(0:1, each = n))        # n respondents to each condition, at random
  y   <- ifelse(z == 1, y1, y0)
  fit <- lm(y ~ z)
  v   <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")
  ci  <- coefci(fit, "z", level = 0.90, vcov. = v, df = Inf)
  c(se = sqrt(v["z", "z"]), reject = ci[1] > 0)
}
sims <- replicate(5000, simulate_experiment())

# the average standard error (Rule 3: 1.32) and the share of rejections (Rule 5: 80%)
rowMeans(sims)
```

### DeclareDesign

The design follows [Declaration 18.1](https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html) in Blair, Coppock, and Humphreys ([2023](#ref-Blair2023)).

```{r}
#| label: sim-ahler-sood-declaredesign
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# the replication as a design: 500 respondents per condition, outcomes with an SD of 20.8
#   within each condition, and a treatment effect of 3.30 (the 80% MDE from Rule 5); analyze
#   each experiment as in the paper (the difference in means, with HC2 standard errors; reject if
#   the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(DeclareDesign)

n    <- 500
sd_y <- 20.8
tau  <- 3.30  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

replication <-
  declare_model(N = 2 * n,
                U = rnorm(N, sd = sd_y),
                potential_outcomes(Y ~ tau * Z + U)) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5)) +
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z, inquiry = "ATE", alpha = 0.10)

# the average standard error (Rule 3: 1.32) and the share of rejections (Rule 5: 80%)
set.seed(1234)
diagnose_design(replication, sims = 5000, bootstrap_sims = FALSE,
                diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
                  se = mean(std.error),
                  power = mean(conf.low > 0)))
```

## R code

```{r}
# R^2 of party identification and partisan strength in the 2020 ANES
r_sq <- summary(lm(ft_outparty ~ pid7 + pid_strength, data = anes))$r.squared
r_sq

# Rule 4: the reduction in the standard error for an R^2 of 5%
1 - sqrt(1 - 0.05)

# footnote 26: the same R^2 in Broockman, Kalla, and Westwood's control and treatment groups
r_sq_control   <- summary(lm(ft_outparty ~ pid7 + pid_strength, data = filter(bkw, treatment == 0)))$r.squared
r_sq_treatment <- summary(lm(ft_outparty ~ pid7 + pid_strength, data = filter(bkw, treatment == 1)))$r.squared
c(r_sq_control, r_sq_treatment)

# footnote 26: their average, and the reduction in the standard error
r_sq_bkw <- mean(c(r_sq_control, r_sq_treatment))
r_sq_bkw
1 - sqrt(1 - r_sq_bkw)
```

## Check by simulation

::: {.panel-tabset group="simulation"}
### Base R

```{r}
#| label: sim-adjusted-5-base-r
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# simulate the replication with Broockman, Kalla, and Westwood's adjustment: 500 respondents per
#   condition, outcomes with an SD of 20.8 within each condition, a control variable with an R^2
#   of 5%, and a treatment effect of 3.20 (the 80% MDE from Rule 5); analyze each experiment as
#   in the paper (OLS with the control variable and HC2 standard errors; reject if the lower
#   bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors
library(lmtest)    # confidence intervals with robust standard errors

set.seed(1234)
n    <- 500
sd_y <- 20.8
r_sq <- 0.05
tau  <- 3.20  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

simulate_experiment <- function() {
  x   <- rnorm(2*n)                                # the control variable
  u   <- rnorm(2*n)
  y0  <- sd_y*(sqrt(r_sq)*x + sqrt(1 - r_sq)*u)    # potential outcomes under control (x explains
  y1  <- y0 + tau                                  #   a share r_sq of the variance)...and under treatment
  z   <- sample(rep(0:1, each = n))                # n respondents to each condition, at random
  y   <- ifelse(z == 1, y1, y0)
  fit <- lm(y ~ z + x)
  v   <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")
  ci  <- coefci(fit, "z", level = 0.90, vcov. = v, df = Inf)
  c(se = sqrt(v["z", "z"]), reject = ci[1] > 0)
}
sims <- replicate(5000, simulate_experiment())

# the average standard error (Rules 3 and 4: 1.28) and the share of rejections (Rule 5: 80%)
rowMeans(sims)
```

### DeclareDesign

The design follows [Declaration 18.1](https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html) in Blair, Coppock, and Humphreys ([2023](#ref-Blair2023)), with a control variable.

```{r}
#| label: sim-adjusted-5-declaredesign
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# the replication with Broockman, Kalla, and Westwood's adjustment as a design: 500 respondents
#   per condition, outcomes with an SD of 20.8 within each condition, a control variable with an
#   R^2 of 5%, and a treatment effect of 3.20 (the 80% MDE from Rule 5); analyze each experiment
#   as in the paper (OLS with the control variable and HC2 standard errors; reject if the lower
#   bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(DeclareDesign)

n    <- 500
sd_y <- 20.8
r_sq <- 0.05
tau  <- 3.20  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

replication_adj <-
  declare_model(N = 2 * n,
                X = rnorm(N),  # the control variable, which explains a share r_sq of the variance
                U = rnorm(N),
                potential_outcomes(Y ~ tau * Z + sd_y * (sqrt(r_sq) * X + sqrt(1 - r_sq) * U))) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5)) +
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z + X, .method = lm_robust, se_type = "HC2", term = "Z",
                    inquiry = "ATE", alpha = 0.10)

# the average standard error (Rules 3 and 4: 1.28) and the share of rejections (Rule 5: 80%)
set.seed(1234)
diagnose_design(replication_adj, sims = 5000, bootstrap_sims = FALSE,
                diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
                  se = mean(std.error),
                  power = mean(conf.low > 0)))
```
:::
:::

```{r}
# footnote 27: R^2 of the pre-treatment measure within each condition (Rule 4 uses the R^2
#   within condition, so both regressions include indicators for the condition)
fit_pre  <- lm(post_ft_outparty ~ condition + pre_ft_outparty, data = pilot)
fit_cond <- lm(post_ft_outparty ~ condition, data = pilot)
r_sq_pilot <- 1 - sum(resid(fit_pre)^2)/sum(resid(fit_cond)^2)
```

## Check by simulation

::: {.panel-tabset group="simulation"}
### Base R

```{r}
#| label: sim-rule-6-base-r
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# simulate the two studies from Rule 6: outcomes with an SD of 20.8 within each condition and a
#   treatment effect of 3, with 1,047 respondents per condition and no control variables, and
#   with 995 respondents per condition and a control variable with an R^2 of 5%; analyze each
#   experiment as in the paper (OLS, with the control variable when there is one, and HC2
#   standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval is above zero)

library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors
library(lmtest)    # confidence intervals with robust standard errors

set.seed(1234)
sd_y <- 20.8
tau  <- 3  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

simulate_experiment <- function(n, r_sq) {
  x   <- rnorm(2*n)                                # the control variable
  u   <- rnorm(2*n)
  y0  <- sd_y*(sqrt(r_sq)*x + sqrt(1 - r_sq)*u)    # potential outcomes under control (x explains
  y1  <- y0 + tau                                  #   a share r_sq of the variance)...and under treatment
  z   <- sample(rep(0:1, each = n))                # n respondents to each condition, at random
  y   <- ifelse(z == 1, y1, y0)
  fit <- if (r_sq > 0) lm(y ~ z + x) else lm(y ~ z)
  v   <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")
  ci  <- coefci(fit, "z", level = 0.90, vcov. = v, df = Inf)
  c(se = sqrt(v["z", "z"]), reject = ci[1] > 0)
}
simulate_study <- function(n, r_sq) rowMeans(replicate(5000, simulate_experiment(n, r_sq)))

# the average standard error (Rules 3 and 4: 0.91 in both studies) and the share of rejections
#   (Rule 6: 95%)
rbind(without_controls = simulate_study(n = 1047, r_sq = 0),
      with_controls    = simulate_study(n = 995,  r_sq = 0.05))
```

### DeclareDesign

The design follows [Declaration 18.1](https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html) in Blair, Coppock, and Humphreys ([2023](#ref-Blair2023)).

```{r}
#| label: sim-rule-6-declaredesign
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# the two studies from Rule 6 as designs: outcomes with an SD of 20.8 within each condition and
#   a treatment effect of 3, with 1,047 respondents per condition and no control variables, and
#   with 995 respondents per condition and a control variable with an R^2 of 5%; analyze each
#   experiment as in the paper (OLS with the control variable, which explains nothing in the
#   first study, and HC2 standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence
#   interval is above zero)

library(DeclareDesign)

n    <- 1047
sd_y <- 20.8
r_sq <- 0
tau  <- 3  # smallest substantively meaningful effect

study <-
  declare_model(N = 2 * n,
                X = rnorm(N),  # the control variable, which explains a share r_sq of the variance
                U = rnorm(N),
                potential_outcomes(Y ~ tau * Z + sd_y * (sqrt(r_sq) * X + sqrt(1 - r_sq) * U))) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5)) +
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z + X, .method = lm_robust, se_type = "HC2", term = "Z",
                    inquiry = "ATE", alpha = 0.10)

# the two studies: the design above, and the design with 995 respondents per condition and an
#   R^2 of 5%
studies <- redesign(study, n = c(1047, 995), r_sq = c(0, 0.05), expand = FALSE)

# the average standard error (Rules 3 and 4: 0.91 in both studies) and the share of rejections
#   (Rule 6: 95%)
set.seed(1234)
diagnose_design(studies, sims = 5000, bootstrap_sims = FALSE,
                diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
                  se = mean(std.error),
                  power = mean(conf.low > 0)))
```

## R code

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
# footnote 12: Rule 1 compared to simulated experiments that use the estimated SE
#   (balanced design, normal outcomes, constant treatment effect)
set.seed(1234)

# design
n     <- 50                # respondents per condition
sigma <- 1                 # SD of the outcome within each condition
se    <- 2*sigma/sqrt(2*n) # true SE (Rule 3)
tau   <- 2.5*se            # treatment effect, so that tau/SE = 2.5

# simulate experiments; reject if the lower bound of the 90% CI is above zero
#   - for a difference in means, the HC2 SE is sqrt(s1^2/n + s0^2/n)
simulate_experiments <- function(n_exp) {
  y0 <- matrix(rnorm(n_exp*n, mean = 0,   sd = sigma), nrow = n_exp)
  y1 <- matrix(rnorm(n_exp*n, mean = tau, sd = sigma), nrow = n_exp)
  row_var <- function(y) rowSums((y - rowMeans(y))^2)/(n - 1)
  tau_hat <- rowMeans(y1) - rowMeans(y0)
  se_hat  <- sqrt(row_var(y1)/n + row_var(y0)/n)
  tau_hat - 1.64*se_hat > 0
}
reject <- map(rep(10000, 100), simulate_experiments) %>% unlist()  # 1,000,000 experiments

# power from Rule 1 and simulated power
power_rule_1 <- 1 - pnorm(1.64*se, mean = tau, sd = se)
power_sim    <- mean(reject)
c(rule_1 = power_rule_1, simulation = power_sim)

# difference (percentage points)
100*abs(power_sim - power_rule_1)
```
:::

```{r}
# footnote 17: the pooled SD exceeds the within-condition SD by sqrt(1 + (tau/sigma)^2/4)
inflation <- function(d) sqrt(1 + d^2/4)

# power predicted with the pooled SD when the true power is 80%
predicted_power <- function(d) 1 - pnorm(qnorm(0.95) - (qnorm(0.95) + qnorm(0.80))/inflation(d))

# small effect (0.2): inflation of the SD and SE (%), of the sample size (%), predicted power
100*(inflation(0.2) - 1)
100*(inflation(0.2)^2 - 1)
predicted_power(0.2)

# large effect (0.8)
100*(inflation(0.8) - 1)
100*(inflation(0.8)^2 - 1)
predicted_power(0.8)
```

## Check by simulation

::: {.panel-tabset group="simulation"}
### Base R

```{r}
#| label: sim-interaction-base-r
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# simulate Robbins et al.'s 2 x 2 factorial design: outcomes with an SD of 2.0 within each
#   condition, an interaction of 0.67, and 223 respondents per condition (for 80% power) or 389
#   (for 95%); analyze each experiment as in the paper (OLS with the two treatments and their
#   interaction, with HC2 standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence
#   interval for the interaction is above zero)

library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors
library(lmtest)    # confidence intervals with robust standard errors

set.seed(1234)
sd_y  <- 2.0
delta <- 0.67  # smallest substantively meaningful interaction

simulate_experiment <- function(n) {
  condition <- sample(rep(1:4, each = n))    # n respondents to each of the four conditions, at random
  z1  <- as.numeric(condition %in% c(2, 4))
  z2  <- as.numeric(condition %in% c(3, 4))
  y   <- delta*z1*z2 + rnorm(4*n, mean = 0, sd = sd_y)   # the main effects are zero; they do not
  fit <- lm(y ~ z1*z2)                                   #   affect the interaction's SE or power
  v   <- vcovHC(fit, type = "HC2")
  ci  <- coefci(fit, "z1:z2", level = 0.90, vcov. = v, df = Inf)
  c(se = sqrt(v["z1:z2", "z1:z2"]), reject = ci[1] > 0)
}
simulate_study <- function(n) rowMeans(replicate(5000, simulate_experiment(n)))

# the average standard error (Rule 3, modified for interactions: 0.27 and 0.20) and the share of
#   rejections (Rule 6, modified for interactions: 80% and 95%)
rbind(n_223 = simulate_study(n = 223),
      n_389 = simulate_study(n = 389))
```

### DeclareDesign

The design follows [Declaration 18.1](https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html) in Blair, Coppock, and Humphreys ([2023](#ref-Blair2023)), extended to a 2 × 2 factorial design.

```{r}
#| label: sim-interaction-declaredesign
#| message: false
#| cache: true
# Robbins et al.'s 2 x 2 factorial design: outcomes with an SD of 2.0 within each condition, an
#   interaction of 0.67 (the main effects are zero; they do not affect the interaction's SE or
#   power), and 223 respondents per condition (for 80% power) or 389 (for 95%); analyze each
#   experiment as in the paper (OLS with the two treatments and their interaction, with HC2
#   standard errors; reject if the lower bound of the 90% confidence interval for the
#   interaction is above zero)

library(DeclareDesign)

n     <- 223
sd_y  <- 2.0
delta <- 0.67  # smallest substantively meaningful interaction

factorial <-
  declare_model(N = 4 * n,
                U = rnorm(N, sd = sd_y),
                potential_outcomes(Y ~ delta * Z1 * Z2 + U,
                                   conditions = list(Z1 = c(0, 1), Z2 = c(0, 1)))) +
  declare_inquiry(interaction = mean((Y_Z1_1_Z2_1 - Y_Z1_0_Z2_1) - (Y_Z1_1_Z2_0 - Y_Z1_0_Z2_0))) +
  declare_assignment(Z1 = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5),                # n respondents to each of
                     Z2 = block_ra(blocks = Z1, prob = 0.5)) +       #   the four conditions
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z1 + Z2)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z1 * Z2, .method = lm_robust, se_type = "HC2", term = "Z1:Z2",
                    inquiry = "interaction", alpha = 0.10)

# the average standard error (Rule 3, modified for interactions: 0.27 and 0.20) and the share of
#   rejections (Rule 6, modified for interactions: 80% and 95%)
set.seed(1234)
diagnose_design(redesign(factorial, n = c(223, 389)), sims = 5000, bootstrap_sims = FALSE,
                diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
                  se = mean(std.error),
                  power = mean(conf.low > 0)))
```
:::
:::
